_comment: Every entry is a file that already exceeded 400 lines when it was recorded.
Entries may only shrink. Lower them with `npm run check:file-size -- --update`
after a file gets smaller; raising one is a hand edit so it shows up in review.
A brand-new entry requires `--update --seed-new` explicitly (#1289); plain
--update never adds a file that was not already in this ledger.
An entry that reaches the threshold must be deleted, not set to the threshold.

kernel.js.why: Kernel is the public compatibility facade and composition root for the v1 runtime: it assembles Graph, MemoryStore, PluginManager, VerifyService and the ephemeral sandbox Kernel. Moving those constructions outward would leak runtime assembly into callers; further size reduction is still owed where cohesive seams can be extracted without increasing coupling. Review alongside #2127 successor decomposition work.

lib/learn-use-case.js.why: Kept whole on purpose (#2198, 2026-09-26). executeLearn holds the knowledge family's eight graph sinks (addNode 3, addEdge 4, addTag 1), and their admission is a transitive claim: this module exports only runLearnUseCase and kernel.js is its only caller, so every sink sits behind kernel.learn's admit(). test/kernel-mutation-admission.test.js and test/mutation-admission-boundary.contract.test.js assert exactly that. Moving any sink-bearing step into a sibling module gives that step an export, i.e. a second way into the sinks, and would weaken the admission guarantee to make the line count smaller. The non-sink helpers are already small; splitting only them would not reach 200.

lib/memory-store.js.why: Kept as the thin facade over its delegates (#2129, 2026-09-26). 971 -> 594 by moving logic into memory-* delegate modules; cross-module private calls are 0. What remains is the public MemoryStore surface (facade methods and their JSDoc) plus the _*StoreApi()/_*ReadContext() builders, and ten test/memory-*-delegation-contract.test.js files pin exactly that shape in this file: each delegate required once here, each facade body, and exact call-site counts. Moving a builder into its delegate needs private-state promotions (_findMemory, _snapshotInMemoryState, _restoreInMemoryState, _makeMemoryKey) and duplicated edges, adding more coupling than it removes; a prototype-mixin split broke 25 of those contracts.
